skill.name: jadx
skill.description: Guide jadx-based Android APK decompilation, deobfuscation, code search, and authorized security analysis through CLI and GUI workflows.
skill.summary: Turn Android DEX bytecode into searchable Java source for authorized analysis.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline formatting, and security-search terms. Confirmed risks include network scanning, testing extracted credentials against devices, and storing sensitive results in plaintext files.

remediation.issue: The workflow recommends testing extracted credentials against IoT devices.
remediation.suggestion: Remove credential reuse instructions, or require documented target authorization and isolated lab devices before any authentication test.

remediation.issue: The integration section recommends network scanning for device enumeration.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict scanning to explicit user-provided targets, require authorization confirmation, and use conservative discovery settings.

remediation.issue: Security searches write possible secrets and credentials to plaintext files.
remediation.suggestion: Redact sensitive values, apply restrictive permissions, define retention limits, and avoid saving full secrets unless required.

content.user_title: Decompile and Analyze Android APKs with jadx
content.value_statement: Reviewing Android bytecode manually makes application behavior and security weaknesses hard to understand. This skill guides jadx decompilation, code search, deobfuscation, and structured APK analysis.
actual_capabilities: Provides jadx CLI commands for APK decompilation, deobfuscation, resource extraction, fallback handling, and Gradle project export.
Explains the generated Java source, Android manifest, resources, assets, and package structure.
Supplies focused searches for credentials, endpoints, storage risks, WebView settings, cryptography, SQL use, and authentication logic.
Documents jadx GUI navigation, full-text search, cross-references, and export workflows.
Supports batch APK processing and complementary analysis with apktool.
Offers troubleshooting for obfuscation, memory limits, slow processing, and incomplete decompilation.
limitations: Requires jadx, a Java runtime, sufficient disk space, and write access on the local system.
Decompiled Java is approximate and may be incomplete, incorrect, or uncompilable.
Heavy obfuscation, packing, native code, and anti-tampering controls can limit results.
The skill does not prove vulnerabilities or replace authorized runtime validation.

use_cases.title: Review a mobile application
use_cases.description: Decompile an authorized APK and inspect authentication, storage, WebView, cryptography, and network code.

use_cases.title: Recover application behavior
use_cases.description: Trace activities, services, resources, and API clients when original source code is unavailable.

use_cases.title: Map IoT companion APIs
use_cases.description: Identify device endpoints, discovery mechanisms, and protocol logic inside an authorized companion application.

prompt_templates.title: Decompile an APK
prompt_templates.prompt: Decompile [APK path] into [output directory] with jadx. Use deobfuscation, explain each command, and summarize the generated source and resource folders.

prompt_templates.title: Run a focused security review
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [APK path] for hardcoded secrets, insecure storage, WebView risks, and weak cryptography. Save only redacted findings and cite relevant classes.

prompt_templates.title: Trace APIs and authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Decompile [APK path], identify API endpoints, and trace authentication from user input to network requests. Explain uncertainty caused by decompilation or obfuscation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare complementary outputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare jadx and apktool output for [APK path]. Map code, resources, and protocol behavior, then propose authorized runtime checks without testing live credentials.

output_examples.input: Analyze sample.apk for secrets and insecure storage.
output: Potential secret references were listed with values redacted.
Storage findings identified affected classes and included verification notes.

output_examples.input: Trace the login flow and API endpoints in companion.apk.
output_examples.output: The report maps login activities to authentication classes and endpoint definitions, then marks uncertain decompiler output for runtime validation.

output_examples.input: Prepare a batch review of three authorized APK files.
output_examples.output: The plan assigns separate output directories, uses quoted paths, limits stored secrets, and produces one findings summary per application.

best_practices: Confirm ownership or written authorization before decompiling or testing an APK.
Use deobfuscation and cross-check important findings against smali or authorized runtime evidence.
Redact credentials and restrict access to decompiled source and findings files.
anti_patterns: Do not test extracted credentials against live systems without explicit authorization.
Do not treat decompiled Java as exact original source or final vulnerability proof.
Do not distribute proprietary decompiled source, embedded secrets, or private application data.

faq.question: What does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires jadx, a compatible Java runtime, disk space, and permission to write the output directory.

faq.question: Does it support jadx GUI?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains GUI navigation, search, cross-references, decompilation views, and export options.

faq.question: Can it recover the original source code?
faq.answer: No. Jadx produces approximate Java that can differ from the original and may contain errors.

faq.question: Can it analyze obfuscated applications?
faq.answer: Yes, but results vary. Deobfuscation can improve names while protected code may remain incomplete or unclear.

faq.question: Does it perform dynamic testing?
faq.answer: No. It can propose authorized runtime checks, but separate tools and controlled environments are required.

faq.question: Is APK decompilation always permitted?
faq.answer: No. Analyze only applications you own or have permission to assess, and follow applicable licenses and laws.
